hero.headline: Zelensky warns of major Russian attacks within 48 hours
hero.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects Russia to launch significant attacks within the next two days.
hero.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he is bracing for a major attack from Russia that he expects to occur within the next 48 hours. The warning is based on intelligence shared by the US and European allies.

Zelensky said the attacks are expected to happen at night, either on the current evening or the following evening. He did not specify the nature or location of the anticipated attacks.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal negotiated by US envoys
cards.teaser: President Trump has asked for amendments to the agreement his envoys reached with Iranian counterparts, according to a senior administration official and a seco.
cards.body:
President Trump met with advisers in the Situation Room on Friday to review a framework agreement his envoys had negotiated with Iran. According to officials, Trump asked for amendments to strengthen several provisions in the deal, particularly those concerning Iran's nuclear material.

The requested modifications have triggered a new round of negotiations between the US and Iran. If finalized, the agreement would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Neither the White House nor Iranian officials have publicly disclosed the specific terms under discussion or a timeline for reaching a final agreement.

cards.headline: UN adds Israeli and Russian forces to sexual violence blacklist
cards.teaser: The United Nations placed Israeli and Russian security forces on its annual list of parties suspected of sexual violence during conflict.
cards.body:
The United Nations has added Israeli and Russian security forces to its annual blacklist for the first time, documenting patterns of sexual violence during conflict. The report includes allegations of rape against detained Palestinians.

The UN's list identifies 77 government and non-government parties credibly suspected of sexual violence in conflict zones. The inclusion of Israeli and Russian forces represents a significant expansion of the blacklist's scope.

cards.headline: Israeli soldiers describe ongoing killings in Gaza despite ceasefire
cards.teaser: Troops shared rare firsthand accounts with journalists about their experiences in Gaza during what officials call a ceasefire.
cards.body:
Israeli soldiers have provided rare firsthand accounts to journalists describing ongoing military operations in Gaza despite the government's characterization of a ceasefire. One soldier directly challenged the terminology, telling reporters that calling the situation a ceasefire is inaccurate.

These accounts from troops on the ground offer an unusual perspective on military operations in the territory. An Israeli commander separately stated that Hezbollah had developed plans for attacks on Israel similar to those carried out by Hamas.

cards.headline: Japan defense minister rejects militarism accusations, criticizes China's military expansion
cards.teaser: Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi denied accusations of new militarism while pointing to China's military arsenal in pointed remarks.
cards.body:
Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi rejected Chinese accusations of new militarism, asserting that Japan remains a peace-loving nation. He criticized China for expanding its military capabilities without sufficient transparency, marking some of Tokyo's most direct comments yet on the dispute over regional military buildups.

Under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's leadership, Japan has accelerated its shift toward a more active defense policy, moving away from the pacifist stance it has maintained since World War II. Despite Beijing's criticism of Tokyo's increasingly assertive security approach, Koizumi pledged Japan would continue strengthening its military capabilities.

cards.headline: Colombian voters choose president as violence overshadows election
cards.teaser: Voters went to the polls in an election marked by a resurgence of political violence and competing visions for the country.
cards.body:
Colombians voted in a presidential election overshadowed by a resurgence of political violence. The contest pitted left-wing and right-wing candidates against each other, with differing visions for addressing the country's decades-long armed conflict.

The election drew international attention, including accusations of foreign interference. Ecuador's leader Daniel Noboa faced criticism for offering to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing presidential candidate ahead of the vote.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo kills at least 245, WHO chief visits affected region
cards.body:
The World Health Organization chief has arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo as an Ebola outbreak continues to spread across the region. Health officials confirm that at least 245 people are suspected to have died from the virus, with 246 suspected cases reported so far in Ituri province.

The medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières has described the spread as deeply alarming. The organization is among several aid agencies working to support health workers who lack adequate equipment to respond to the crisis.

The outbreak centers on Ituri province, a conflict-affected area that shares borders with Uganda and South Sudan. The province presents particular challenges for disease control due to its role as a mining hub where thousands of people work in close proximity daily. Uganda's health ministry confirmed the virus has already spread beyond the DRC, reporting that a 59-year-old man died in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the affected region.

The WHO estimates the death rate at between 30 and 50 percent among confirmed cases. As one WHO official stated, "It's huge. It means that up to five out of 10 people are likely to die."

A significant concern is the strain of Ebola detected in the outbreak. The DRC's national research laboratory identified the Bundibugyo strain in 13 of 20 samples tested. Unlike the more common Zaire strain, for which vaccines exist, there is no licensed vaccine for Bundibugyo. Only two previous outbreaks of this strain have been recorded, in 2007 and 2012.

Ebola spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, including blood and vomit from infected people, as well as through contact with dead bodies during funeral preparations. The virus causes severe illness with high fatality rates.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention have expressed concern about further spread, particularly given the high population movement between affected areas and neighboring countries. The organization has convened an urgent regional meeting with authorities from the DRC, Uganda and South Sudan, along with the WHO and pharmaceutical companies.

The DRC has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976. According to global health experts, multiple factors contribute to these recurring outbreaks. Close contact with animal reservoirs, likely bats or primates, combined with movement between rural and urban areas, tropical climate conditions, and extensive rainforest coverage create conditions that facilitate transmission.

Health workers responding to the outbreak face significant risks from potential virus exposure while working with limited protective equipment and medical supplies. Protecting healthcare workers remains essential to maintaining treatment capacity and preventing transmission within medical facilities. Aid agencies continue working to contain the virus and treat affected populations as cases spread across the region.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested across France after Champions League celebrations turn violent
cards.teaser: Police arrested hundreds after Paris Saint-Germain fans celebrated their Champions League victory over Arsenal with flares and clashes.
cards.body:
Hundreds of people were arrested across France after celebrations following Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory over Arsenal turned violent. Thousands of police officers worked to control unrest as crowds of fans took to the streets, with some firing flares.

Police in Paris arrested more than 130 people as jubilant PSG supporters spilled onto the streets. The arrests occurred nationwide as authorities responded to clashes and disorder during the victory celebrations.

cards.headline: Japan defense minister rejects militarism accusations, criticizes China's military expansion
cards.teaser: Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi denied accusations of new militarism while pointing to China's military arsenal in pointed remarks.
cards.body:
Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi rejected Chinese accusations of new militarism, asserting that Japan remains a peace-loving nation. He criticized China for expanding its military capabilities without sufficient transparency, marking some of Tokyo's most direct comments yet on the dispute over regional military buildups.

Under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's leadership, Japan has accelerated its shift toward a more active defense policy, moving away from the pacifist stance it has maintained since World War II. Despite Beijing's criticism of Tokyo's increasingly assertive security approach, Koizumi pledged Japan would continue strengthening its military capabilities.

cards.headline: Taiwan debates security measures after Chinese-born woman accused of infiltration
cards.teaser: A case involving a Chinese-born woman has sparked discussion about defending democracy while avoiding profiling of mainland spouses.
cards.body:
Taiwan is grappling with how to strengthen democratic defenses following accusations that a Chinese-born woman attempted infiltration. The case has sparked debate over security policies targeting mainland Chinese spouses of Taiwanese citizens.

Officials are working to balance legitimate security concerns against potential discrimination toward the thousands of mainland spouses currently living in Taiwan. The situation underscores wider concerns about possible influence operations originating from Beijing.

cards.headline: Ukraine denies deliberately hitting Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant with drone
cards.teaser: Kyiv rejected Russian claims that a Ukrainian drone deliberately struck the nuclear facility in occupied territory.
cards.body:
Ukraine denied that its forces deliberately targeted the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant after Russia said a Ukrainian drone struck the facility. The International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed that a drone attack hit a turbine building at the plant.

Ukrainian defense forces rejected Russian claims about the attack on the nuclear power plant unit. The facility has been under Russian control since early in the conflict and remains a source of concern for nuclear safety officials.

cards.headline: Colombian voters choose president as violence overshadows election
cards.teaser: Voters went to the polls in an election marked by a resurgence of political violence and competing visions for the country.
cards.body:
Colombians voted in a presidential election overshadowed by a resurgence of political violence. The contest pitted left-wing and right-wing candidates against each other, with differing visions for addressing the country's decades-long armed conflict.

The election drew international attention, including accusations of foreign interference. Ecuador's leader Daniel Noboa faced criticism for offering to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing presidential candidate ahead of the vote.

cards.teaser: Troops shared rare firsthand accounts with journalists about their experiences in Gaza during what officials call a ceasefire.
cards.body:
Israeli soldiers have provided rare firsthand accounts to journalists describing ongoing military operations in Gaza despite the government's characterization of a ceasefire. One soldier directly challenged the terminology, telling reporters that calling the situation a ceasefire is inaccurate.

hero.headline: Eleven workers killed in Washington state paper mill chemical accident
hero.body:
One Dead, One Injured in Washington Skydiving Accident

A skydiving accident in Washington state resulted in one death and one injury after two jumpers collided midair during a group jump, authorities said this week.

The Adams County Sheriff's Office responded Sunday evening to a call reporting two skydivers needing medical attention at West Plains Skydiving near Longview. Upon arrival, deputies learned that a midair collision had occurred during a scheduled group jump, leaving one skydiver dead and another injured.

The two skydivers involved were identified as Randy Hubbs of the Kennewick area and Nicole Klein of the Colville area. According to preliminary findings from the investigation, the collision happened during the descent phase of the jump.

Following the impact, Hubbs became incapacitated and lost control of his parachute canopy. Staff members at the drop zone observed and tracked Hubbs from approximately 500 feet above ground level as he drifted north away from the designated landing zone. Witnesses reported that he appeared unresponsive with his head and arms down before disappearing beyond a hill to the northeast.

Klein sustained injuries that required additional medical treatment at a facility.

West Plains Skydiving provided details about how the collision occurred. According to the company's statement, at approximately 1,000 feet above the ground, the two parachutes came into contact with neither jumper aware of the other's position.

Weather conditions were not considered a contributing factor in the incident, according to the sheriff's office. A total of 11 individuals participated in the jump operation.

Both skydivers had extensive experience. Hubbs had completed more than 800 previous jumps, while Klein had completed approximately 900 jumps.

In a statement, West Plains Skydiving expressed grief over the loss. "The Skydive West Plains community is mourning the loss of a friend who has been part of the drop zone family for nearly a decade," the company said. The statement added that the team's thoughts were with Klein and her family as she recovers from her injuries.

The Adams County Sheriff's Office said investigators were continuing to look into the circumstances surrounding the accident. In a statement released Monday, the sheriff's office offered condolences to those affected by the incident.

The investigation remains ongoing as authorities work to determine the exact sequence of events that led to the collision.

cards.headline: Protesters clash with police at New Jersey immigration detention facility
cards.teaser: Violence erupted outside the Delaney Hall facility despite the governor's call for calm, prompting Newark's mayor to impose a curfew.
cards.body:
Protests continued Saturday outside the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey, as a hunger and labor strike by detainees inside reached its ninth day. Detained immigrants are demanding improved conditions and medical care.

On Saturday morning, counterprotesters wearing Trump hats gathered at the facility to show support for Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The two groups faced off across barricades set up by state police, with protesters supporting the detained immigrants and ICE supporters yelling at each other.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Trump administration plans for Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A federal judge stopped Trump administration changes to the Kennedy Center, including plans to add the president's name to the facility.
cards.body:
A federal judge blocked Trump administration plans for the Kennedy Center in Washington. The ruling prevented the administration from adding Trump's name to the performing arts center and stopped a planned closure of the facility.

Protesters gathered at the Kennedy Center to oppose the Trump-led changes. The demonstration turned into what one report described as a party atmosphere. The ruling angered Trump, according to reports about the decision's reception.

cards.headline: Four inmates escape Alabama correctional facility
cards.teaser: Authorities are searching for four inmates who escaped from an Alabama correctional center.
cards.body: Authorities have not released the names of the inmates or details about how the escape occurred. The location of the correctional center within Alabama was not specified in available information.

cards.headline: Trump doctor reports leg swelling and hand bruising but says president in excellent health
cards.teaser: The White House released results from Trump's latest physical examination showing minor issues but an overall assessment of excellent health.
cards.body:
President Trump's doctor declared him in "excellent health" following a routine medical examination, according to a White House memo. Navy Captain Sean Barbabella noted that the 79-year-old demonstrated strong cardiac, pulmonary, neurological and overall physical function.

The doctor recommended that Trump lose weight and increase exercise. The three-page memo released by the White House provided an overview of the president's medical checkup.

cards.headline: Becerra takes lead in California governor race polling
cards.teaser: Xavier Becerra gained support in the latest poll for California governor, with Tom Steyer and Rick Hilton trailing close behind.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra is leading a tight three-way Democratic contest for California governor, alongside fellow Democrat Tom Steyer and Republican Steve Hilton. The race remains highly competitive as voters prepare for the June 2 primary election.

California's political landscape is unusually turbulent heading into the primary. Voters appear frustrated and underwhelmed with their options across multiple races, including the governor's contest, the Los Angeles mayoral battle, and several congressional races that could influence control of the US House in November.

cards.headline: Trump criticizes Pope Leo XIV for meeting with Chicago Mayor Johnson
cards.teaser: President Trump attacked Pope Leo XIV after the pontiff met with Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson during a visit to the city.
cards.body:
President Trump criticized Pope Leo XIV for meeting with Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson. The meeting drew a mixed reaction in Chicago, with some supporting the papal visit and others questioning the choice of meeting participants.

Chicago Teachers Union President Stacy Davis Gates traveled to meet Pope Leo XIV during his visit. The pope received a goodie bag during his time in Chicago. The meeting and related events generated divided responses from Chicago residents and officials.

hero.headline: Anthropic Raises $65 Billion, Valuation Surpasses OpenAI
hero.body:
Anthropic has raised $65 billion in its latest funding round, achieving a post-money valuation of $965 billion and becoming more valuable than OpenAI. The Series H funding round makes the artificial intelligence company one of the most highly valued private technology firms in the world.

The seven cofounders of Anthropic are now collectively worth $116 billion following the funding announcement. The company, which develops AI systems including the Claude language model, has attracted substantial investor interest as competition intensifies in the generative AI sector.

Analyst Dan Ives described Anthropic's growth as representing just the beginning of a broader rally in artificial intelligence investments. The valuation milestone comes as major technology companies and investors pour unprecedented amounts of capital into AI development and infrastructure.

The funding round's scale reflects investor confidence in Anthropic's position within the rapidly expanding AI market. The company has positioned itself as a competitor to OpenAI, which developed ChatGPT and has been valued at lower levels in recent funding activities.

Anthropic's rise in valuation occurs amid increasing demand for advanced AI capabilities across industries. The company has focused on developing what it describes as safer and more reliable AI systems, attracting partnerships with major enterprises and cloud computing providers.

The $965 billion valuation places Anthropic among the most valuable private companies globally, exceeding the market capitalizations of many established public corporations. The funding will support continued expansion of Anthropic's research operations, computational infrastructure, and product development efforts as the company seeks to maintain its competitive position in the AI sector.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Receives National Security Contract Hours Before New Glenn Rocket Explosion
cards.teaser: Blue Origin secured a national security launch task order just hours before its New Glenn rocket exploded at a Florida launch complex.
cards.body:
Blue Origin received a national security launch assignment shortly before its New Glenn rocket exploded during a test on a launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night. The company has since regained access to Launch Complex 36, where the explosion occurred.

The incident represents a significant setback for Blue Origin as it competes with SpaceX for space launch services contracts. The timing of the explosion, occurring just hours after securing the government task order, underscores the challenges the company faces in developing its heavy-lift launch capability.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Diverted After Passenger Attempts Cockpit Breach
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted after a passenger allegedly tried to breach the cockpit, triggering a hijacking alert.
cards.body:
United Airlines Flight 2005 traveling from Chicago to Minneapolis diverted to Madison after a man attempted to access the cockpit during the flight. The incident prompted a hijacking alert and led to the passenger's arrest by the FBI.

The FBI later decided not to pursue charges against the 75-year-old passenger involved in the incident. The flight was safely diverted and landed in Madison, where law enforcement took the passenger into custody before the aircraft continued to its destination.

cards.headline: SoftBank Plans Up to $75 Billion Investment in French AI Data Centers
cards.teaser: SoftBank announced plans to invest up to $75 billion to build AI data centers in France, creating what would be Europe's largest AI facility.
cards.body:
SoftBank plans to invest up to €75 billion to build AI data centers in France. The project will develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity, making it Europe's largest AI infrastructure complex.

The investment underscores the intensifying competition among technology companies to establish computational infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence development and deployment across Europe.

cards.headline: China Factory Activity Declines, Signaling Economic Headwinds
cards.teaser: Factory activity in China worsened, providing a warning sign for the country's broader economic outlook.
cards.body:
Manufacturing activity in China deteriorated according to recent data, indicating potential weakness in the world's second-largest economy. The decline in factory output suggests reduced industrial demand and production.

The worsening factory conditions add to concerns about China's economic trajectory. Manufacturing activity serves as a key indicator of overall economic health, with declines typically preceding broader slowdowns in growth and employment.

cards.headline: China's Biotechnology Industry Gains Ground in Drug Development
cards.teaser: Clinical trials in China are drawing attention at an international oncology conference as the country's biotechnology sector expands rapidly.
cards.body:
Chinese clinical trials received significant attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago, underscoring the country's expanding role in pharmaceutical research. The visibility reflects China's growing capabilities in biotechnology and drug development.

China's surge in biotech investment and clinical research is reshaping the global pharmaceutical landscape. This advancement has raised concerns in the United States about the country's declining dominance in biotechnology and pharmaceutical innovation.

cards.headline: Ferrari Faces Criticism Over First Electric Vehicle Design
cards.teaser: Ferrari's debut electric vehicle, the Luce, has generated backlash from critics who say the design departs from the brand's traditional identity.
cards.body:
Ferrari introduced the Luce, its first electric vehicle intended to compete with Chinese EV manufacturers, but the model has drawn sharp criticism. Some observers have accused the Italian automaker of abandoning the core design principles that have defined Ferrari vehicles.

The brand's move into electric vehicles comes as legacy automakers seek to challenge Chinese competitors in the EV market. The negative reception to the Luce highlights the challenges traditional performance car manufacturers face when transitioning to electric powertrains while maintaining brand identity.

hero.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, triggering sonic boom across New England
hero.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating a powerful sonic boom that was heard across a wide region, according to Nasa.

The fireball broke up just after 2pm local time at an altitude of 40 miles while traveling at 75,000 miles per hour. The explosion produced a blast equivalent to 300 tons of TNT, Nasa's deputy news chief Jennifer Dooren confirmed.

The sonic boom was detected across a vast geographic area. Witnesses reported hearing and feeling the explosion from multiple states, with reports coming from as far away as Delaware and extending north into parts of Canada. The meteor's path took it over populated areas of the northeastern United States, making it visible and audible to hundreds of people across the region.

The loud noise startled residents throughout New England who were uncertain about its cause. Many turned to social media and contacted local authorities to report the unusual phenomenon. Some described the experience as terrifying, with the sudden sound jolting people awake or interrupting their daily activities.

Meteors entering Earth's atmosphere at extremely high speeds create intense friction with air molecules, generating tremendous heat. When a meteor breaks apart in the atmosphere, it produces shock waves that reach the ground as sonic booms. These sounds can travel considerable distances depending on atmospheric conditions and the size of the meteor.

No confirmed reports of debris reaching the ground or causing damage have been released. Most meteors burn up completely in the atmosphere before any fragments can reach the surface. When fragments do survive atmospheric entry, they typically fall across remote areas where they go undiscovered.

Nasa noted that while the meteor was significant in size and speed, such events occur periodically around the world. Most space objects are small enough to disintegrate harmlessly above the planet. According to scientific research, approximately 17,000 meteorites fall to Earth annually, though most are small and undetected.

Authorities have not issued any warnings or alerts related to the meteor. The phenomenon, while startling to those who experienced it, posed no threat to public safety. The event served as a reminder that Earth regularly encounters space debris as it travels through the solar system. Nasa confirmed the first visibility of the meteor occurred above the region before it fragmented during its descent through the atmosphere.

cards.headline: Nvidia-powered Windows PCs set to debut next week
cards.teaser: The first Windows computers using Nvidia processors are scheduled to be unveiled next week, according to multiple reports.
cards.body:
Microsoft and Nvidia are preparing to launch the first Windows PCs powered by Nvidia chips, with an announcement expected next week. The companies have been teasing the development on social media ahead of Nvidia's GTC event.

The new N1X laptop processors are being developed in collaboration with Arm. This marks a significant shift for the Windows PC market, which has historically depended on processors from Intel and AMD.

cards.headline: SoftBank plans up to $75 billion investment in French data centers
cards.teaser: The Japanese investment firm announced a major commitment to expand data center infrastructure in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank plans to invest up to €75 billion in French data centers, with the goal of developing and operating up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity in the country.

The investment underscores growing demand for computing infrastructure to support cloud services and artificial intelligence applications across Europe.

cards.headline: James Bond game '007: First Light' records strong first-day sales
cards.teaser: The new James Bond video game has achieved significant commercial success in its first 24 hours of release.
cards.body:
Developer IO Interactive has brought its stealth expertise to the James Bond franchise with '007: First Light'. The game follows a young Bond before he earns his 00 status, taking a different approach than simply adapting the studio's Hitman formula. IO Interactive's experience with globetrotting assassination gameplay, cinematic presentation, and its in-house Glacier engine provided a foundation for the project.

The game has become a major commercial success, with strong 24-hour sales figures. Available on PC, Xbox, and PlayStation 5, it has been recognized as a significant achievement for the Bond video game franchise, which had lacked a major entry in recent years.

cards.headline: Blue moon visible Sunday night across multiple continents
cards.teaser: The second full moon of May, known as a blue moon, is rising this weekend.
cards.body:
A rare blue micromoon is visible Sunday night. The phenomenon occurs when two full moons happen in the same calendar month, with May's second full moon appearing smaller in the sky due to its distance from Earth.

Multiple news organizations provided viewing guidance for the event. The Washington Post noted beautiful conditions with a bright moon, while CNN and PBS offered details on timing and visibility. The Australian Broadcasting Corporation explained why the full moon represents a rare occurrence.

cards.headline: AC unveils new Cobra coupe with 720 horsepower V8 engine
cards.teaser: Britain's oldest active carmaker has released a production version of its high-performance sports car.
cards.body:
AC officially debuted a new Cobra coupe featuring a Ford 5.0-liter V8 engine producing up to 720 horsepower. Some variants of the supercharged engine deliver 799 horsepower in the two-seat sports car.

The vehicle is priced at approximately $315,000 to $500,000 depending on configuration. Car and Driver noted the British carmaker's new model draws on the iconic Cobra heritage. Multiple automotive outlets described the supercharged performance as worthy of the nameplate's legacy.

cards.headline: Tunnel project enables rewilding in southern England landscape
cards.teaser: The Hindhead Tunnel has contributed to one of the most successful rewilding efforts in the region.
cards.body:
A lost road helped spark a major rewilding project in southern England. The Hindhead Tunnel eliminated the need for a previous road route, allowing the landscape to be restored.

The project has become one of the most successful rewilding initiatives in southern England. The removal of the road infrastructure created opportunities for habitat restoration and the return of native species to the area.

hero.headline: PSG wins second straight Champions League title in penalty shootout over Arsenal
hero.teaser: Paris Saint-Germain became the second team ever to win consecutive Champions League titles.
hero.body:
Paris Saint-Germain retained the Champions League by defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout in Budapest on Saturday. The victory marks only the second time in the competition's history that a team has won back-to-back championships.

The match went to a shootout after regulation and extra time could not separate the two sides. Arsenal defender Gabriel missed the decisive penalty kick in the shootout that determined the outcome.

For Arsenal, the loss represented a missed opportunity to complete what would have been a historic season. The club had won the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years just days before the Champions League final. Arsenal has never won the European competition and had reached the final only once before, in 2006, when they lost to Barcelona.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta had expressed confidence heading into the match. He emphasized that winning the Premier League had only increased the squad's hunger for more trophies. Arteta told his players they were capable of winning the Champions League after their recent domestic success.

"The ambition is bigger," Arteta said before the match. "We have one, and now we want the second one." He highlighted the team's desire and clarity of purpose, saying he was confident they would be close to winning.

Arsenal forward Bukayo Saka, who had scored in last season's semifinal loss to PSG, expressed belief in the team's chances. He noted that winning the Premier League after finishing second three times in a row had given the players confidence going into the final.

Saka also revealed that Thierry Henry, who was part of Arsenal's team that lost to Barcelona in 2006, had reached out during the week to offer encouragement. Saka said winning the Champions League would have completed a perfect season for the club.

PSG came into the final as the defending champions after winning the competition for the first time the previous year. The French club had defeated Chelsea, Liverpool, and Bayern Munich in the knockout stages on their path to Budapest.

The match marked Arsenal's 63rd game of the season, more than any other team from the top five European leagues. PSG had played 56 matches heading into the final.

The result sparked celebrations in Paris, though the festivities led to significant unrest. Paris police deployed thousands of officers and arrested more than 130 people as crowds gathered around PSG's stadium. Police used teargas to control the crowds, and footage showed brief skirmishes as supporters fired fireworks.

cards.headline: Spurs eliminate defending champion Thunder, advance to NBA Finals
cards.teaser: The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference finals at Paycom Center, eliminating the defending NBA cham.
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference finals on Saturday night, eliminating the reigning champions and advancing to the NBA Finals. Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs with 22 points in the decisive victory.

San Antonio will now face the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio.

cards.headline: Claude Lemieux's family to donate his brain for CTE research
cards.teaser: The former NHL player's brain will go to Boston University's CTE Center for study of repetitive brain injuries.
cards.body:
Claude Lemieux's family announced Saturday that his brain will be donated to the Boston University CTE Center. The donation will support research into chronic traumatic encephalopathy and the long-term effects of repetitive head injuries sustained during athletic careers.

The Boston University CTE Center is a leading research institution studying brain injuries in professional athletes. Lemieux played in the NHL across multiple teams during his professional hockey career.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested in France after Champions League celebrations turn chaotic
cards.teaser: Thousands of police officers responded to unrest as fans celebrated PSG's victory.
cards.body:
Hundreds of people were arrested in France following Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory over Arsenal. The celebrations became unruly as crowds gathered in French cities, with some fans firing flares during the festivities.

Thousands of police officers were deployed to manage the disorder and restore control. PSG secured their Champions League title through a penalty shootout win against Arsenal in Budapest.

cards.headline: Fernando Tatis Jr. ends MLB-worst home run drought with 451-foot blast
cards.teaser: The Padres outfielder hit his first homer of the season against the Nationals.
cards.body:
Fernando Tatis Jr. broke through with a solo home run to left field against the Nationals, ending the longest homer drought in baseball this season. The blast traveled 451 feet, giving the Padres an additional run in the game.

Tatis had not hit a home run through the season's early stages, the worst stretch among any active MLB player. The solo shot marked his first long ball of the year.

cards.headline: Caitlin Clark held to six points in Fever's loss to Fire
cards.teaser: The Indiana star struggled with her shooting in the 100-84 defeat.
cards.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark struggled with her shot Saturday night, scoring just six points in a 100-84 loss to the Fire. The poor shooting performance was one of her lowest-scoring games of the season.

The defensive pressure from the Fire limited Clark's usual offensive output in the 16-point victory.

cards.headline: Tennessee coach Karen Weekly accused of handshake line comment to former player
cards.teaser: Texas Tech player says Volunteers coach told her she made a mistake transferring from Tennessee.
cards.body:
Texas Tech third baseman Taylor Pannell said Tennessee coach Karen Weekly told her during the handshake line that she made a mistake transferring from the Volunteers. The comment came after Tennessee's 2-1 extra-inning victory at the Women's College World Series.

Weekly called the accusation a lie. The exchange has drawn attention to interactions between coaches and former players during the high-stakes softball tournament in Oklahoma.

hero.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remainder of Four Seasons Farewell Tour Due to Health Concerns
hero.body:
Frankie Valli has canceled the remaining dates of the Four Seasons farewell tour to focus on his health. The 92-year-old music legend announced the cancellation, apologizing to fans for the disappointment.

Valli had been touring with the Four Seasons as part of what was billed as a farewell tour. The cancellation affects all remaining 2026 concert dates.

In his announcement, Valli expressed regret to fans who had planned to attend the scheduled performances. The singer said he needed to prioritize his health moving forward.

Valli rose to fame as the lead singer of the Four Seasons in the 1960s, with hits including "Sherry," "Big Girls Don't Cry," and "Can't Take My Eyes Off You." The group became one of the best-selling musical acts of all time, and their story was adapted into the Broadway musical "Jersey Boys."

The farewell tour had been marketed as a final opportunity for fans to see Valli perform live. At 92, Valli had continued to perform despite his advanced age, maintaining an active touring schedule in recent years.

Ticket holders for the canceled shows will need to seek refunds through their point of purchase. The announcement did not provide specific details about the nature of Valli's health concerns or whether the cancellation might be temporary.

Valli's decision to step back from touring comes as he enters his tenth decade. The singer has maintained a presence in popular culture through both his classic recordings and continued live performances over six decades in the music industry.

The Four Seasons' catalog remains influential in American popular music, with their songs continuing to receive airplay and feature in films and television programs. The group was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1990.

cards.headline: Search for Man Believed to Be 'Alaskan Bush People' Star Matt Brown Suspended After Reports He Took His Own Life
cards.teaser: Authorities have suspended their search for a man believed to be reality television personality Matt Brown after reports that he took his own life.
cards.body:
Search efforts for a man believed to be Matt Brown, known for the Discovery Channel series "Alaskan Bush People," have been suspended. Brown's brother Bear reported that Matt had been spotted near a river where police say a man went missing.

Authorities received reports that the individual took his own life. The suspension of the search follows the sighting near the river. Brown appeared on "Alaskan Bush People," which followed the Brown family living in remote Alaska.

cards.headline: Two Films Directed by YouTubers Top Weekend Box Office
cards.teaser: The two highest-grossing films at the box office this weekend were both directed by filmmakers who began their careers on YouTube.
cards.body:
"Backrooms" and "Obsession" claimed the top two positions at the weekend box office, both helmed by filmmakers who built their audiences on YouTube. "Obsession" unseated "The Mandalorian and Grogu" from the number-one spot.

Producer Jason Blum drew parallels between the current success of low-budget horror films and the edgy cinema of the 1970s. Blum and producer James Wan highlighted how YouTube creators are reshaping the horror genre, with word-of-mouth driving these films' commercial success and reinvigorating the industry.

cards.headline: Warner Bros. Pictures Chief Warns Against Cutting Development Budgets for Original Projects
cards.teaser: Michael De Luca cautioned that reducing investment in new material could harm the film industry's creative pipeline.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

Warner Bros. Pictures chief Michael De Luca spoke at the Produced By conference hosted by the Producers Guild of America, warning about the consequences of studios reducing development funds. He said cutting too deeply into development budgets would cause the creative pipeline to dry up.

De Luca described his approach as a relentless pursuit of new talent and fresh voices as a way to refresh the pipeline. He delivered what attendees characterized as a master class in studio leadership during his session at the conference.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Cast Member Over Racial Slur for Second Consecutive Year
cards.teaser: Peacock's reality dating series has dismissed a participant after social media posts surfaced showing the use of a racial slur.
cards.body:
Love Island USA has dismissed cast member Vasana Montgomery following the emergence of social media posts containing racial slurs. The removal comes just two days after the Season 6 cast announcement, with Montgomery excluded from the show's return to Peacock on June 2.

This marks the second consecutive year the reality dating series has removed a participant for using offensive racial language, signaling a pattern the production has addressed through cast dismissals.

cards.headline: Brad Pitt Photographed in Paris After Son Files to Drop His Last Name
cards.teaser: The actor was seen with girlfriend Ines de Ramon following reports that his son Maddox is removing Pitt from his surname.
cards.body:
Brad Pitt and Ines de Ramon were photographed smiling in Paris after news broke that Pitt's son with Angelina Jolie has filed to drop the actor's last name. Maddox Jolie-Pitt filed paperwork to remove Pitt from his surname.

Sources told Us Weekly that Brad Pitt feels hurt by his children dropping his last name and fears becoming permanently disconnected from them. The actor was seen on a date night with de Ramon despite the family developments.

cards.headline: Niall Horan Reflects on Liam Payne's Death in New Interview
cards.teaser: The former One Direction member discussed his late bandmate, who died in 2024 after falling from a hotel in Argentina.
cards.body:
In a recent interview with The Times of London, Niall Horan discussed the death of his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne, who died in 2024 at age 31 after falling from a hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Horan was in Argentina shortly before Payne's death.

When reflecting on his late bandmate, Horan described experiencing conflicting emotions. He explained that thinking about Payne brings sadness, but also moments of laughter and fond memories of their time together.

hero.headline: Zelensky warns of major Russian attacks within 48 hours
hero.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects Russia to launch significant attacks within the next two days.
hero.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he is bracing for a major attack from Russia that he expects to occur within the next 48 hours. The warning is based on intelligence shared by the US and European allies.

Zelensky said the attacks are expected to happen at night, either on the current evening or the following evening. He did not specify the nature or location of the anticipated attacks.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal negotiated by US envoys
cards.teaser: President Trump has asked for amendments to the agreement his envoys reached with Iranian counterparts, according to a senior administration official and a seco.
cards.body:
President Trump met with advisers in the Situation Room on Friday to review a framework agreement his envoys had negotiated with Iran. According to officials, Trump asked for amendments to strengthen several provisions in the deal, particularly those concerning Iran's nuclear material.

The requested modifications have triggered a new round of negotiations between the US and Iran. If finalized, the agreement would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Neither the White House nor Iranian officials have publicly disclosed the specific terms under discussion or a timeline for reaching a final agreement.

cards.headline: Justice Department seeks judge's removal from Georgia election case
cards.teaser: The Justice Department asked a federal judge to step aside from a lawsuit against Georgia election officials.
cards.body:
The Justice Department filed a motion on Friday asking a federal judge to recuse herself from overseeing its lawsuit against Georgia election officials. The request argues that the judge's attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis raises questions about her ability to remain impartial.

The filing was submitted to the US District Court. The Justice Department's motion centers on concerns that the judge's participation in the Willis event could compromise her neutrality in the case involving Georgia election officials.

cards.headline: UN adds Israeli and Russian forces to sexual violence blacklist
cards.teaser: The United Nations placed Israeli and Russian security forces on its annual list of parties suspected of sexual violence during conflict.
cards.body:
The United Nations has added Israeli and Russian security forces to its annual blacklist for the first time, documenting patterns of sexual violence during conflict. The report includes allegations of rape against detained Palestinians.

The UN's list identifies 77 government and non-government parties credibly suspected of sexual violence in conflict zones. The inclusion of Israeli and Russian forces represents a significant expansion of the blacklist's scope.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor exits Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped down from the case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who obtained an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped away from the case, according to a court filing. A notice of substitution filed in the Eastern District of North Carolina on Friday stated that Matthew, the prosecutor, would no longer be handling the matter.

Comey faces charges for allegedly threatening the life of President Trump in a since-deleted social media post of seashells. The filing did not provide a reason for the prosecutor's departure from the case.

cards.headline: Immigrant detainees file lawsuit over Texas ICE facility conditions
cards.teaser: Detainees at a Texas immigration facility are suing the federal government over conditions they describe as inhumane.
cards.body:
A class-action lawsuit filed Saturday targets conditions at Camp East Montana, the nation's largest immigration detention facility located in El Paso, Texas. Four detainees are named as plaintiffs representing all current and future civil detainees at the facility.

The suit alleges severe violations of human and constitutional rights, citing deficient medical and mental health care, inappropriate use of force, widespread solitary confinement, inadequate food, disease outbreaks, unsanitary living conditions, and sexual harassment by guards. Legal organizations are pursuing the case against Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor and DHS secretary coordinate on protest response
cards.teaser: New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin reached agreement on handling protests outside a Newark detention center.
cards.body:
New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin found common ground on Saturday after the governor deployed state police to maintain order outside a Newark immigration detention center. The facility has been the site of escalating protests.

Sherrill said New Jersey police officers have responded to protests at the detention center. The coordination between the Democratic governor and the DHS secretary came as the protests intensified at the facility.
